App details

Dialer

An Android phone app for calls, contacts and call history, with configurable automatic redial.

In the worksPlannedAndroid

What it’s for

A complete default phone app for Android, covering everyday incoming, outgoing and ongoing calls. Find people through the dialpad or system contacts, use favorites and call history, choose a SIM and keep call notes. Automatic redial has separate settings for intervals and attempt limits.

Main features

  • Dialpad, T9 contact search and favorites.
  • Incoming and ongoing call controls.
  • Choose a SIM, block numbers and add call notes.
  • Set redial intervals and attempt limits.

This app is planned. The description presents documented plans, not an app available to download. The final design and app still need approval and testing; there is no announced release date.

How to use

Choose Dialer as Android’s default Phone app through the system prompt. Dial a number or search system contacts with the keypad, select a SIM and manage incoming or ongoing calls. Use favorites, call history, speed dial and blocked numbers. For automatic redial, set an interval and attempt limit, start it deliberately and stop it when needed; call notes remain separate.

Important limits

Calling depends on telephony service and the default Phone role. Role or permission loss limits affected features. No call recording, transcription, community spam database or remote caller identification is planned.

Offline use, permissions and purchases

Contact browsing and local notes can work without a JN86 server. Actual calls need the device’s telephone service and network; Play purchase or restore may also need internet.

Android 7.0 or newer is the common planned baseline. Individual sensor and platform features still depend on the device.

Permissions

Default Phone role and relevant Phone, Contacts and Call Log access are requested through Android under applicable rules. Permission denial must leave an understandable limited state; no surveillance audio permission is planned.

Local data

The app uses system contacts and call log rather than a duplicate full database. Its notes, block rules, redial history, SIM choices and UI settings would stay locally. No contacts or call notes are uploaded to JN86; system call-log deletion is separate.

Advertising and purchases

The plan is ad-free. Ordinary calling is free. Free redial allows up to 20 attempts and 10 call notes; one-time Premium increases these limits, adds note reminders and deeper layout options. There is no subscription or call recording.

First version and later ideas

The functions above belong to the documented plan for the first version. Features mentioned below as excluded or later ideas are not promised as current capabilities.

The full phone app and configurable redial are planned. Free and one-time Premium have different redial and note limits, described above; additional themes and custom colour picker are excluded.

Availability

This app is being created. The features described here are planned; it is not yet available to download.
